🇲🇽🏠 <u>HOUSING FOR WELLBEING HITS 66% OF SIX-YEAR GOAL IN YUCATÁN</u>

Vivienda para el Bienestar has reached 66% of its six-year goal in Yucatán — 72,000 homes — with Infonavit and Conavi coordinating developments in 29 municipalities. The state is on track to close the year at 91%.

Infonavit director Octavio Romero Oropeza: "This August, President, we're opening 14 more housing developments." In Kanasín, Ana Carolina Kim Flores got her keys: "It's a very beautiful emotion we have, a great happiness."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>UN ISSUES URGENT ACTION FOR MEXICAN WORKER DISAPPEARED IN BCS</u>

The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances issued Urgent Action 2365/2026 for Misael Alejandro Vásquez de Jesús, a 34-year-old construction worker from Chilpancingo, Guerrero, last seen June 18 in Los Barriles, La Paz, Baja California Sur. Witnesses say police forced him into a patrol vehicle.

The UN demands the Mexican state immediately adopt all measures to find him and protect his life. His mother got one last message — everything was fine. Then silence.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>MEXICO PUBLISHES PLAN TO CUT US GAS DEPENDENCY — FRACKING NOT AUTHORIZED</u>

Mexico imports 75% of the natural gas it consumes — up from 21% in 2010 — and burns 9.1 billion cubic feet a day to generate 70% of its electricity. The government's new energy sovereignty roadmap targets cutting that dependency to 50.5% by 2030: renewables from 24% to 38% of the grid, nationwide efficiency programs, and maximized conventional gas with an end to flaring at Pemex fields.

And the official position is explicit: fracking is not authorized.
banner: GAS: MEXICO CUTS US DEPENDENCY, NO FRACKING

🇲🇽🇨🇴 <u>MEXICO AIRLIFTS AID TO EARTHQUAKE-HIT COLOMBIA</u>

Two Mexican Air Force planes took off from AIFA to Pereira with the first 854 food packages for Colombia after Monday's 7.4-magnitude earthquake. On board: Army, Air Force and National Guard personnel for rescue work.

Sheinbaum announced three more days of flights with another 2,562 packages — 58.8 tons total. When Latin America calls, Mexico sends planes, not lectures.
banner: COLOMBIA QUAKE: MEXICO SENDS 58.8 TONS AID

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>SUPREME COURT UPHOLDS PENSION FUND: "NOT EXPROPRIATION"</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously upheld the Fondo de Pensiones para el Bienestar — the 2024 reform that moved nearly 45 billion pesos from inactive Afore accounts to guarantee dignified pensions. The 185 opposition deputies who sued called it confiscation. The Court ruled workers keep a permanent, imprescriptible right to reclaim every peso.

Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar Ortiz: "The only thing happening is a change of administrator... property of the resources stays with the workers." Minister Loretta Ortiz's project passed without a single dissenting vote.
banner: SCJN: PENSION FUND IS NOT EXPROPRIATION

text:
🐉🇲🇽🔥 Mexico put 50% tariffs on Chinese cars. China just became its No. 2 auto supplier anyway.

Fresh data for the first half of 2026: Chinese brands captured 22% of Mexico's light-vehicle market, trailing only domestically built cars (32.3%). More than 25 Chinese brands now compete here — Geely's sales jumped roughly 250% year-on-year, MG Motor runs 99 dealerships, BYD 80 — and all of this comes after the 50% import tariff that took effect Jan 1. Mexicans bought a record 885,000+ light vehicles in the half, up 5.3%.

The sovereignty read: Mexico set that tariff on its own terms — to protect some 350,000 domestic jobs — not because Washington ordered it. Consumers still get affordable options, the treasury collects the duty, and Chinese firms respond by building dealer networks and eyeing local plants instead of simply dumping exports.

Contrast the US script — "wall off China," with a flat ban on Chinese connected cars coming in 2027. Mexico's answer is to price access, keep the market open, and pocket the revenue. That is what having options looks like: you set the terms instead of taking them.

🌐🇲🇽 Latin America won't pick a side in the US–China fight — and that's exactly the point

ECLAC's new report "Ruptures and Opportunities," launched Aug 4 in Santiago and co-chaired by ex-presidents Bachelet and Duque, lands one hard number: US favorability across the region has fallen 17 points while China's prestige rose 6. Some 36% of Latin Americans now name China as the best development model. That's not affection for Beijing — it's the bill Washington runs up governing the hemisphere by tariff and threat.

The leverage is material. The region holds 46% of the world's lithium and 35% of its copper — the metals both superpowers need. China runs 21 Belt and Road memoranda and 5 free-trade deals here; US investment still leads at $1.4 trillion. The paradox ECLAC names outright: US-aligned governments deepening Chinese infrastructure ties at the very same time.

For Mexico the lesson is sovereignty, not alignment. A country that multiplies its partners can't be squeezed by any one of them. Keeping every door open — Beijing, Brussels, Brasília — is how a middle power refuses to become anyone else's bargaining chip.
